solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Look agitated following massacre

indicators.note: following says the word for agitated comes after the word for massacre

parts.note: to butcher people is to massacre them
shook means agitated, as in all shook up

explanation.surface: Someone appears visibly shaken after witnessing a slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTCHER'S HOOK is Cockney rhyming slang (hook rhymes with look), so 'have a butcher's' means 'have a look'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang pairs the phrase with the word it rhymes with, so it stands for a glance.

clue.text: Batters food on counters

explanation.surface: A cook coats food in batter and lays it out on the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To batter is to strike repeatedly, the verb sense; the noun sense is a self-service spread of food laid out on tables.

clue.text: Ingredient of healthy meals?

indicators.note: an ingredient is one part of a mixture, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question about what goes into wholesome cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb is a common culinary ingredient, used to season many healthy dishes.

clue.text: Carefully selects tools to support labourer

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first, holding it up

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
picks are pointed digging tools

explanation.surface: A foreman carefully chooses which implements his worker will be given.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose things individually and with care is to select them by hand, one at a time.

clue.text: Ready reckoner is proof enough — initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A ready reckoner is all the evidence anyone needs.
explanation.walkthrough: A ready reckoner is a book of precalculated tables; 'Ready' is split off from it to be the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is mature enough to eat is ready, and so is anything prepared for action.

clue.text: Longed for Attila, say, to suppress rampant greed

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down, and in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Attila was a famous leader of the Huns, so he is an example of one

indicators.note: rampant means running wild, so the letters of greed are rearranged

explanation.surface: The barbarian warlord tried to curb his rampant avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: Attila the Hun led the Huns, so 'say' marks him as an example; 'rampant' shuffles the greed letters, and 'to suppress' places them below in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungered for and longed for are synonyms, both meaning craved or yearned for something.

clue.text: Honours even at first, but carrying too much weight

parts.note: OBEs are British honours, awards of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A sporting contest finishes level early on but one side is overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese describes someone who is seriously overweight, carrying far more body fat than is healthy.

clue.text: A vehicle loaded into orbiter may supply snack

indicators.note: loaded into says the first pieces are put inside the word for orbiter

parts.note: the moon orbits the Earth
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Space travellers load a rover onto a spacecraft that will carry provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small almond biscuit, the sort of thing eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Dishes delayed in case of prayers

indicators.note: in says the word for delayed goes inside the other letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: something delayed is late

explanation.surface: Food arrives late because grace is being said first.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates are flat dishes from which food is served or eaten.

clue.text: The precursor to fire in which one cooks

definitions.text: The precursor to fire in which one cooks

parts.words: The precursor to fire in which one cooks
parts.note: the saying 'out of the ... into the fire' names the cooking vessel you leave just before reaching the flames

explanation.surface: A riddle about what comes just before the fire in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: This shallow pan is used for cooking with fat, and the proverb places it just before the fire.

clue.text: Rejected story covering degree communication

indicators.note: covering says the reversed word wraps around the degree
rejected means sent back, so the word for story is read in reverse

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a falsehood
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: An editor turns down a tale that includes a mention of someone's academic qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' reverses only the story word, and 'covering' then wraps it around the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message, a form of communication.

clue.text: Grant relief for part of complex empty

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tax relief is granted for part of a building complex standing empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to free them from an obligation, granting them relief from it.

clue.text: Broadcast late (mainly) and never to the point

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged
mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A programme aired late and never really on topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims LATE to LAT; 'Broadcast' then shuffles LAT and NEVER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relevant is pertinent, bearing directly on the matter in hand.

clue.text: Stiffener for the top of the bill before church

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: the star of a show is the act at the top of the bill

explanation.surface: A headline performer needs something to steady the nerves before going to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is used to stiffen fabric such as shirt collars, so it is a stiffening agent.

clue.text: Pepper that's sort of special around mid-Wales

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the central letter
sort of hints at a loose version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the middle letter of the word Wales

explanation.surface: A seasoning with a special flavour found in the heart of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' turns SPECIAL into ALSPICE, which goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: This spice is also known as Jamaica pepper, the dried berry of a Caribbean tree.

clue.text: International organisation looking embarrassed and bad-tempered

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
cross means angry or bad-tempered

explanation.surface: A global body looking flushed and irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanitarian movement founded in Geneva operates worldwide, an international organisation.

clue.text: Two firms admitting hotel student consumed sweet

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the hotel letter goes inside the firms

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, and two firms give it twice
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Two businesses let a hotel student in, and the student devoured a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate is a sweet, a confection made from cocoa.

clue.text: Get a tube in order to find bread in Paris

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means rearranging them into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A traveller takes the Underground to buy a loaf in the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The long thin French loaf is the bread you would buy in Paris.

clue.text: Merry king's rule for cabbage in salad

parts.note: Old King Cole was a merry old soul in the nursery rhyme, so this is his possessive
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A jolly monarch decrees that cabbage must go in the salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the 'merry old soul' of the English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: This dish is shredded raw cabbage in dressing, so it is cabbage served as a salad.

clue.text: First of children with spouse is nearly 6

indicators.note: first of asks for the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: hubby is a colloquial word for husband, a spouse

explanation.surface: The eldest child and partner are nearly six years old.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to 6-down, OBESE: being plump is nearly being obese.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and slightly fat is almost, but not quite, seriously overweight.

clue.text: Royal Navy reserve finally in bed — for a bit of brass

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A naval reservist ends up in bed with a piece of brass.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument is a small valved member of the brass family, so one piece of the brass section.

clue.text: They may lose heart with harangues from such rulers

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letters of the word are removed

parts.note: rants are long angry speeches, harangues

explanation.surface: Subjects may become demoralised by the ranting of despots.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of THEY is HE; removing it leaves TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrants are cruel and oppressive rulers who hold absolute power.

clue.text: Blow share on dinner — with no starter

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the second piece after the first
with no starter means the first letter is dropped, playing on a meal's first course

parts.note: supper is an evening meal, a dinner
a cut is a share, as in a cut of the profits

explanation.surface: Someone splits the cost of an evening meal but skips the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a punch thrown upward, a blow in boxing.

clue.text: Compass needed in mountains

explanation.surface: A navigational instrument is needed for walking in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in its sense of scope or extent means the same as range; a range is also a chain of mountains.

clue.text: More self-possessed in jail

explanation.surface: Someone becomes calmer once in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler is the comparative of cool, meaning calm; it is also slang for a prison cell.

clue.text: Shelf life begins with slight advantage

indicators.note: begins asks for the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: an edge is a small advantage over a rival

explanation.surface: Life on the shelf starts with a small head start.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow horizontal surface projecting from a wall, a shelf.

clue.text: Cure for a dry sense of humour

explanation.surface: A remedy for someone whose wit is too dry.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure meat is to preserve it with salt; salt also means sharp, dry wit, as in Attic salt.

clue.text: Food account put into good French

indicators.note: put into says the account letters go inside the French word

parts.note: bon is the French word for good

explanation.surface: A bill for food is placed into a good French restaurant's ledger.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pork, an item of food.

clue.text: Where refreshments end a great wrong?

indicators.note: wrong means amiss or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about where snacks put an end to a great injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is elliptical: a place where refreshments (are served).
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor garden serving tea and light refreshments is where you would find them.

clue.text: All the same?

parts.note: something all the same is never any smaller, so the word means not one bit less, read as three words

explanation.surface: A question asking whether everything is identical.
explanation.definitionFit: All the same is an idiom meaning however or despite that, a synonym for this adverb.
